evidence.quote: I see the risks to employment as tilted to the downside and risks to inflation to the upside.
With the unemployment rate at 4.3 percent, the labor market is softening, which suggests that, left unsupported, it could experience stress.
This change moved our policy rate closer to a more neutral stance while maintaining a balanced approach to promoting our dual-mandate objectives.
I expect the disinflation process to resume after this year and inflation to return to the 2 percent target in the coming years.
The uptick in the unemployment rate suggests that demand has fallen by a bit more than supply and that the downside risks to employment are rising.
